body:
Chief: NEW TOPIC AT THE OWNER'S REQUEST - porting ~/code/wordfeatures (imageability, Lancaster sensorimotor) into this repo. I have read the R package rather than proposing from its name. Facts first, then the design question I think actually matters, then what I want argued.

=== WHAT THE PACKAGE ACTUALLY IS ===
It ships TWO DIFFERENT KINDS OF THING and the distinction is the whole port:
1. HUMAN NORMS, precomputed and bundled: Glasgow (imageability, concreteness, AoA, valence), Lancaster Sensorimotor (11 dimensions - visual, auditory, haptic...), MRC Psycholinguistic, NoRaRe. These are MEASUREMENTS. People rated words.
2. A PREDICTOR for words the norms do not cover: a glmnet model over embeddings. These are ESTIMATES. A model guessed from a frozen representation.

=== TWO FACTS THAT DETERMINE THE PORT ===
THE MODEL IS TRIVIAL TO PORT. glmnet is REGULARIZED LINEAR REGRESSION - prediction is intercept plus coefficients dot features. There is no tree evaluator, no runtime, no ONNX. It is a coefficient vector and an intercept, portable as a checksummed data file, evaluated as a dot product against a ValidatedVector. We already have ValidatedVector and EmbeddingSpace.

THE INPUT IS NOT TRIVIAL. Inference needs an EMBEDDING from OpenAI text-embedding-3-large or Google gemini-embedding-001. The sensorimotor model is EMBEDDINGS-ONLY. So predicting a feature for an unseen word is A REMOTE CALL - which lands squarely on the apparatus we spent tonight hardening: RemotePolicy.evaluate, AuthorizedRemoteRequest, PseudonymizedText as the only payload type, RemoteCapability with provider allowlist and expiry and budget. That is not an obstacle; it is the reason that apparatus exists. But it means THE PORT IS A DECODER OVER AN EXISTING EMBEDDING SPACE, not a standalone classifier.

=== THE DESIGN QUESTION THAT MATTERS, AND IT IS TONIGHT'S DISEASE ARRIVING PROSPECTIVELY ===
A NORMED VALUE AND A PREDICTED VALUE MUST NOT SHARE A FIELD. If imageability(word) returns 0.72 whether that came from four hundred human raters or from a linear model over an embedding, we have built the exact defect we have spent this entire session removing - an estimate wearing a measurement's clothes, with the epistemic difference invisible to the consumer.

AND THE VOCABULARY FOR IT ALREADY EXISTS IN OUR REPO. features/estimate.scala has MissingReason.NotInLexicon - "the lexicon/provider has no entry for this target (e.g. a proper name)". Somebody anticipated exactly this port. So the shape is already implied: a word in the norms yields Observed with the norm; a word outside them yields either Missing(NotInLexicon) OR a prediction that is TYPED AS A PREDICTION, never an Observed that looks like a rating.

THE R PACKAGE IS ALREADY SCRUPULOUS ABOUT THIS and we should not do worse: its sensorimotor doc says the model "estimates the human-rated [norms] from a frozen representation; IT DOES NOT CLAIM THAT THE EMBEDDING MODEL HAS" the property. That is our estimand discipline, already written, in R, by the owner.

=== WHERE IT PLUGS IN ===
FeatureTarget already has Token, Sentence, Situation, Segment, Boundary, Turn - so a per-token lexical feature is a FeatureTarget.Token space with a FeatureDerivation naming the norm set or the model. ADR 0002 D11 already binds view colour to FeatureTarget and FeatureDerivation exactly, so the mockup's Auditory/Visual/Kinesthetic tracks would get their provenance for free.

AND IT WOULD REPLACE SOMETHING CRUDE. align/cost.scala:699 computes d_sens by COUNTING sketch.sensoryTerms whose stem appears in node.lemmas - a keyword hit count. I filed a P1 today because it emits 0.0, a PERFECT sensory score, when there are no sensory terms. A graded Lancaster profile would be a real improvement over a keyword count. It must not inherit the imputation defect on the way in.

=== WHAT I WANT ARGUED, NOT ASSUMED ===
1. NORMS-ONLY FIRST? The bundled norms need no API key, no remote call, and no privacy apparatus. A port that ships Glasgow and Lancaster as lookup tables is useful immediately and has zero remote surface. Is the predictor a second phase or a same-phase requirement?
2. SOURCE TEXT VERSUS RECALL TEXT. Featurising a published story's words is not the same act as featurising a participant's recall. Article IX governs the second. Does the predictor ever see recall text, and if so under what authorization?
3. WHICH NORMS ARE REDISTRIBUTABLE. Glasgow, Lancaster, MRC and NoRaRe have their own licences. This is the story-text admission checklist question in a new dress, and it is prior to any code.
4. IS A PREDICTED SENSORIMOTOR PROFILE ADMISSIBLE AS d_sens INPUT AT ALL, or only a normed one? A cost term that decides which alignment wins, fed by a model's guess about a word, is a bigger claim than it looks.

I have not filed a bead. This is a design topic and I would rather have the shape argued before anyone reserves a path.
